newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares set new record high on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares set new record high on U.S. data.

text.p: Brussels Bel-20 shares set a new all-time high on Tuesday after U.S. December economic data calmed investors' fears of an imminent U.S. interest rate hike.
Dealers expected the Bel-20 to hit 2,000 in coming days if the dollar remained strong and fundamentals remained in check.
"We could go a bit higher, but one of these days we'll see the top and lower-than-expected year results will cause a serious correction," said one trader.
The blue-chip Bel-20 closed up 0.76 percent, or 14.94 points, at 1,991.50 after earlier touching an all-time intraday high at 1,998.02.
"A serious correction is an exaggeration because there is no alternative for the moment (than to stay in stocks) as the dollar remains strong with interest rates stable," said another trader.
Investors welcomed U.S. reports that confirmed growth in the U.S. economy has not triggered higher inflation.
Chemical and drugs group UCB rallied in today's trade, closing up 4.4 percent at 90,200 francs.
Dealers said UCB's blockbuster anti-allergy drug Zyrtec had made investors pick up the stock with the expectation that sales would be strong in the U.S.
Analysts expected UCB to get clearance later this year to sell Zyrtec in Japan, the world's second biggest pharmaceutical market.
"In the long run there is no reason why UCB will not have the same success in Japan like we've seen in the U.S.," said analyst Jurgen Fryges at KB-Securities.
Elsewhere chemicals firm Solvay climbed 2.99 percent to 22,400 francs.

Dealers said Solvay was benefitting from renewed interest in chemical stocks in Europe and Solvay's increased focus on its pharmaceutical division and particularly in its development of anti-depressant drugs.
Elsewhere chemical firm Tessenderlo closed up 5.1 percent to 15,425 francs as investors grabbed what they said was a high quality cyclical stock made attractive by recent acquisitions.
"It's been picking up companies recently, which is reducing the cyclical exposure of the stock," said analyst Luc Van Der Elst at G-Securities.
